title: gSTEP variant screen — ranking STEPtag binding by fluorescence (ΔF/F0)
summary: Rank a handful (2–8) of gSTEP biosensor variants by their relative binding to STEPtag. Each variant, fixed at 75 nM, is challenged with one shared STEPtag dilution series so all variants are compared on the same axis; variants are ranked by fluorescence dynamic range (ΔF/F0) and apparent affinity. Tuned for comparison across variants, not a precise single-pair Kd.
source_citation: Eason et al., ACS Synth. Biol. 2020, DOI 10.1021/acssynbio.0c00407
estimated_duration: ~3 h for up to 8 variants on 1–2 plates (excludes protein expression/purification)

materials.name: Purified gSTEP variants to screen (His-tagged, IMAC-purified, buffer-exchanged, A280-quantified)
materials.provenance_note: 75 nM final per well is stated in the source; applied identically to every variant so ΔF/F0 is comparable.

materials.name: Binding partner (titrant): STEPtag
materials.provenance_note: User selected STEPtag as the common partner for the screen.

materials.name: Control protein: bovine serum albumin (BSA)
materials.provenance_note: BSA named as a control protein in the source; defines nonspecific ΔF.

equipment: Multichannel pipette (to dispense the shared STEPtag series identically across variants)
Reagent reservoir / dilution plate for the shared master series

steps.title: Prepare assay buffer
steps.instruction: Prepare 20 mM sodium phosphate buffer with 50 mM NaCl, pH 7.4; filter-sterilize. Used as both storage and assay diluent.

critical_parameters.name: Buffer composition
critical_parameters.value: 20 mM sodium phosphate, 50 mM NaCl, pH 7.4

steps.title: Normalize and prepare each variant at 75 nM
steps.instruction: Quantify each purified gSTEP variant by A280 (ProtParam extinction coefficients) and dilute every variant to an identical 75 nM working concentration in assay buffer. Equal biosensor concentration across variants is what makes ΔF/F0 comparable.

critical_parameters.name: gSTEP concentration
critical_parameters.provenance_note: Stated; held identical across all variants.

critical_parameters.name: Number of gSTEP variants
critical_parameters.provenance_note: User is screening a handful of variants; sets plate layout and whether a second plate is needed.

critical_parameters.name: gSTEP working-solution volume per variant
critical_parameters.provenance_note: Scaling per variant: 6 titrant points x 3 replicates = 18 wells; gSTEP is dispensed at 50 uL/well as a 2x working stock (the shared STEPtag series supplies the other 50 uL), so 18 x 50 uL = 0.9 mL ~= ~1 mL including dead volume. Verify against your final layout.

warnings: Keep variants on ice and shielded from light until dispensed.

steps.title: Prepare ONE shared STEPtag master dilution series
steps.instruction: Because affinities are unknown and the goal is ranking, prepare a single wide STEPtag dilution series and apply it identically to every variant. Run a quick pilot on one representative variant first to center the bracket.

critical_parameters.name: Shared STEPtag titration bracket
critical_parameters.provenance_note: Wide bracket chosen because expected Kd is unknown; a sparse 6-point series is enough to rank variants. Center it after the pilot; flag to verify.

substeps.instruction: Pilot: run one representative variant across the full ~3 nM–10 uM range to find where its response transitions, then keep or narrow the bracket for the full screen.
substeps.provenance_note: Pilot needed because Kd is unknown.

substeps.instruction: Prepare the master series once in a reservoir/dilution plate so every variant sees the identical STEPtag concentrations (multichannel transfer).
substeps.provenance_note: A single shared series removes between-variant pipetting variance from the ranking.

warnings: If any variant's ΔF/F0 is still rising at the top concentration, its binding is weaker than the bracket covers — extend the top point before ranking it.

steps.title: Lay out the plate(s)
steps.instruction: For each variant, combine 75 nM gSTEP with the shared STEPtag series across a row (or block) of the Fluotrac plate. Add one BSA control series per plate and, per variant, buffer-only and gSTEP-only (F0) wells. If variants span two plates, repeat one reference variant on both plates for normalization.

critical_parameters.name: Assay volume per well
critical_parameters.provenance_note: User selected 100 uL/well (scale choice; not specified in the source).

critical_parameters.name: Replicates
critical_parameters.provenance_note: ‘a minimum of three replicates’ stated; a first-pass screen can drop to 2 to fit more variants per plate.

critical_parameters.name: Control titration (BSA)
critical_parameters.provenance_note: One control-protein titration per plate defines nonspecific ΔF for background subtraction; per-plate rather than per-variant saves wells.

critical_parameters.name: Per-plate reference variant
critical_parameters.value: repeat one variant on every plate
critical_parameters.provenance_note: Anchors plate-to-plate normalization when a screen spans multiple plates.

warnings: Mix gently; bubbles corrupt fluorescence reads.

steps.title: Equilibrate
steps.instruction: Incubate all plates under identical conditions to reach binding equilibrium before reading.

critical_parameters.name: Equilibration time and temperature
critical_parameters.provenance_note: Not stated in the source. Standard-practice default; keep it identical across all variants and plates so ΔF/F0 is comparable. Verify equilibrium is reached for your tightest binders.

steps.title: Read fluorescence (fixed gain across the whole screen)
steps.instruction: Read every plate on the Tecan Infinite M1000 with excitation at 485 nm and emission at 515 nm. Set the gain once on the brightest bound well across ALL variants and hold it fixed for every plate.

critical_parameters.name: Fixed reader gain across variants
critical_parameters.value: set once on the brightest well; hold constant for all plates
critical_parameters.provenance_note: Comparability requirement for a screen: if gain varies between variants or plates, ΔF/F0 is no longer comparable. Verify no wells saturate at the chosen gain.

warnings: A different gain per variant invalidates the ranking — this is the most common screen mistake.

steps.title: Rank the variants
steps.instruction: Subtract the BSA control background, then for each variant compute ΔF/F0 = (F_saturated − F0)/F0 as the primary ranking metric. Optionally fit each sparse series to the ligand-depletion Hill equation for an apparent Kd as a secondary sort. Rank variants by ΔF/F0, then apparent affinity.

critical_parameters.name: Primary ranking metric (ΔF/F0)
critical_parameters.provenance_note: For a variant screen, dynamic range (ΔF/F0) is the primary readout; the paper reports ΔF/F0 alongside Kd. Apparent Kd from a sparse fit is a coarse secondary sort only.

critical_parameters.name: Fitting model
critical_parameters.value: Hill equation accounting for ligand depletion
critical_parameters.provenance_note: The source specifies this fit (cites reference 35). Use total concentrations; depletion is modeled.

warnings: Tight binders (apparent Kd ≤ ~75 nM) are ligand-depletion-limited at 75 nM biosensor: their apparent Kd is compressed and rankings among the very tightest binders may be unreliable. Lower the biosensor concentration to separate them.

assumptions_log.basis: User selected STEPtag for the screen.

open_questions: Expected Kd is unknown — the pilot on one variant is required to center the shared bracket before the full screen.
Ligand depletion at 75 nM biosensor compresses apparent Kd for tight binders (Kd ≤ ~75 nM); to rank the tightest binders precisely, repeat them at a lower biosensor concentration.
Replicate count: 3 gives the paper's rigor; 2 fits more variants per plate for a first-pass rank — your call on the precision/throughput trade.

On a live run, Phase-2 web_search would ground the ΔF/F0 screening convention, the sparse-titration spacing, and the depletion caveat in specific citations (upgrading the best_practice/default_verify items to verified literature_grounded).
